 proof fn always_double<T>(ex: Execution<T>, p: TempPred<T>)
     requires always(p).satisfied_by(ex),
-    ensures always(always(p)).satisfied_by(ex),
+    ensures always(always(p)).satisfied_by(ex),
 {
+
+    // `always(p)` means: for all i, p holds at the suffix shifted by i.
+    // To show `always(always(p))`, we must show that for all j,
+    // `always(p)` holds at suffix shifted by j.
+    //
+    // Unfolding the definition:
+    //   always(always(p)).satisfied_by(ex)
+    //     == (forall k. always(p).satisfied_by(ex.suffix(k)))
+    // and always(p).satisfied_by(ex.suffix(k))
+    //     == (forall i. p.satisfied_by(ex.suffix(k + i))).
+    // Using the premise, we directly get `p.satisfied_by(ex.suffix(k+i))`.
+    assert forall |k: nat| #[trigger] always(p).satisfied_by(ex.suffix(k)) by {
+        // Fix an arbitrary k and show `always(p)` holds at ex.suffix(k)`.
+        assume k: nat;
+        assert forall |i: nat| #[trigger] p.satisfied_by(ex.suffix(k + i)) by {
+            // From the premise we know: for all t, p holds at ex.suffix(t).
+            // Choose t = k + i.
+            assert p.satisfied_by(ex.suffix(k + i)) by {
+                // Reuse the premise directly.
+                assert always(p).satisfied_by(ex) by {
+                    // This is exactly the requirement.
+                }
+                // Since always(p).satisfied_by(ex) is `forall t. p.satisfied_by(ex.suffix(t))`,
+                // instantiate with t = k + i.
+            }
+        };
+    };
 }
*** End Patch
